facts.label: Strongest contrary evidence and limitations (evidence, risk mechanism, consequence)
facts.text: - Evidence: the covenant disclosure for the current facilities is a single summary sentence, [10-K p:113] "the key financial covenants prohibit the Consolidated First Lien Leverage Ratio for the reference period ended on such date from exceeding 7.75 to 1.00 as of any date of determination with step-downs for the first three years to 7.25 to 1.00, 6.75 to 1.00 and 6.25 to 1.00." Mechanism: the sources do not state whether the test applies at all times or only when revolver usage passes a threshold (the superseded facility had a usage trigger, [10-Q 2025-12-31 p:25]), nor the step-down dates. Consequence: covenant headroom analysis cannot be completed from the pack; the reported Credit Agreement Net Leverage Ratio is a different, net, all-debt measure from the first lien test and may not be used as covenant headroom. - Evidence: [10-Q 2026-09-30 p:27] "The Company was in compliance with covenants under the AR Securitization Facility after receiving a waiver of the Delinquency and Default Ratios from the lender effective September 30, 2026." Mechanism: a waiver was needed to avoid breach at the quarter end and the facility was amended again on October 29, 2026, but the new ratio levels and the waived ratio levels are not stated. Consequence: receivables-facility trigger risk is visible but unquantifiable. - Evidence: the annual report covers only a short post-acquisition stub ([10-K p:57]), and the quarterly reports show a large increase in net sales against prior-year columns. Mechanism: year-over-year and annual comparisons mix perimeters. Consequence: modules must label period and perimeter on every figure and use the pro forma and Legacy CMCO disclosures only as attributed management or unaudited pro forma data. - Evidence: [10-Q 2026-09-30 p:11] preliminary purchase price allocation, with goodwill adjusted in the quarter. Mechanism: goodwill, intangibles and amortization may still change. Consequence: asset-based and amortization-sensitive measures carry a measurement-period limitation.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is usable but must be read in two layers. Reported (GAAP) layer: the business more than doubled in size on the Kito Crosby close (H1 FY2027 net sales 1,070,746 against 496,967 in H1 FY2026), but it is loss-making after amortization, interest and deal costs (H1 FY2027 net loss attributable to the Company 114,262; FY2026 net loss 229,535 including a 200,000 goodwill impairment), operating cash flow is small (H1 FY2027 21,065) and FY2026 operating cash flow was negative (146,211), reflecting acquisition and divestiture related cash payments. Lender-defined layer: the Credit Agreement Trailing Twelve Month Adjusted EBITDA of 467,796 at September 30, 2026 normalises a full year of Kito Crosby, the divestiture and cost synergies, and gives a Credit Agreement Net Leverage Ratio of 4.9x. The first layer is audited or filed; the second is a management reconciliation of a defined credit agreement term and is supporting evidence only. Debt is 2,412,308 (carrying value, including finance lease and the receivables facility) at September 30, 2026, up from 2,393,007 at March 31, 2026. About 1,551,465 of principal is floating rate against 965,000 of interest rate swap notional, so roughly 586,465 is unhedged on the figures supplied. Liquidity is 531,980 with the revolver commitment (500,000) the only meaningful undrawn source. The covenant package (first lien leverage test, maximum 7.75x stepping down) looks roomy against the 4.9x total net measure on an indicative reading, but trigger, step-down dates and exact definition are not supplied, so headroom is not calculable. Confidence in the base is Medium: the filed statements are internally consistent (debt carrying value ties to principal less unamortized costs; the lender-defined EBITDA reconciles line by line), while the credit documents, discrete Q4 FY2026 statements and any ratings are absent.

Adjusted EBITDA also adds back stock-based compensation, which is a cost.

facts.label: Interpretation: evidence, risk mechanism, credit implication
facts.text: - Leverage. Evidence: total debt 2,412,308 against Credit Agreement TTM Adjusted EBITDA of 467,796 (5.16x gross; 4.9x on the company's net definition); total debt at March 31, 2026 was 2,393,007. Mechanism: the measured improvement comes from the earnings base growing into the pro forma figure (441,030 to 467,796) and cash rising, not from repayment, and the earnings base includes assumed synergies. Implication: leverage is sensitive to synergy delivery; a shortfall of 10% in pro forma EBITDA would add roughly 0.6x to gross leverage. That sensitivity is derived and illustrative. - Cover and floating-rate cost. Evidence: H1 FY2027 EBITDA over cash interest of 2.45x; interest and debt expense 95,660 for six months versus FY2027 guidance of 185 to 190 million. Mechanism: floating-rate debt of 1,551,465 with 965,000 hedged leaves about 586,465 exposed to base-rate moves, and the term loan margin was just cut by 50 bps. Implication: a 100 bps rise in base rates would add roughly 5,865 a year on the unhedged amount (derived, illustrative, ignoring the floor and hedge expiries), small against EBITDA but large against free cash flow of 4,601 in H1 FY2027. - Cash generation. Evidence: H1 FY2027 operating cash flow 21,065 and free cash flow 4,601 after cash deal and integration costs of 24,300 (company-stated for the first half, [EX Nov03 p:3]); cash interest paid 90,921. Mechanism: deal and integration cash costs plus working capital outflows absorb EBITDA. Implication: a 100 bps rise in base rates would add roughly 5,865 a year on the unhedged amount (derived, illustrative, ignoring the floor and hedge expiries), small against EBITDA but large against free cash flow of 4,601 in H1 FY2027.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Columbus McKinnon is a century-and-a-half-old US industrial manufacturer of hoists, lifting and securement hardware, precision conveyors, digital power controls and actuators, sold mainly through distributors and crane builders. On February 3, 2026 it bought Kito Crosby Limited from funds associated with KKR in an all-cash deal, financed by a 900,000 senior secured notes issue, a 1,650,000 term loan, a revolver draw and 800,000 of Series A preferred shares sold to CD&R XII Keystone Holdings, L.P. (the CD&R Investor). To gain regulatory approval it also sold its U.S. power chain hoist and chain operations on March 4, 2026 and used the proceeds to prepay the term loan. The resulting credit profile is a larger, more consumables-weighted business that is loss-making on a reported basis, carries total debt of 2,412,308 at September 30, 2026 and 531,980 of liquidity (the same figures as the CP-1 handoff), and has a large investor with board and preemptive rights whose preferred shares accrue a 7% payment in cash or in kind ahead of common shareholders. Business risk is moderated by breadth of product, brand and geography, and by consumable-type replacement demand that management describes (Management Language); it is raised by cyclical exposure to industrial activity, the distributor channel, the integration of a business of about the same size and a short-tenured finance leadership. Ownership and governance evidence shows supportive documented actions (equity funding, use of divestiture proceeds for debt reduction, in-kind preferred dividends so far) and no documented creditor-adverse or extraction-oriented action, but the legal capacity for such actions depends on credit and indenture documents that are not supplied. Confidence is Medium: the filed business and transaction facts are well sourced, while the executed transaction, investor and financing documents and any customer concentration data are missing.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The transaction is the acquisition of 100% of the equity of Kito Crosby Limited from funds associated with KKR, completed on February 3, 2026 after a definitive agreement announced on February 10, 2025. Status: completed; the purchase price allocation remains preliminary and the working capital adjustment is final. Three figures describe its size and they differ: the December 2025 quarterly report describes an all-cash transaction "valued at $2,700,000,000" subject to customary adjustments and regulatory approval ([10-Q Dec25 p:9]); the annual report's allocation table totals 2,811,907 ([10-K p:88]); and the September 2026 quarterly report states the all-cash transaction value as 2,821,907, which includes a 10,000 increase for the final working capital adjustment, paid after September 30, 2026 ([10-Q Sep26 p:9]). The last two reconcile by the stated adjustment (2,811,907 plus 10,000, derived); the headline-to-consideration difference is not explained in the pack and is logged as a conflict, not reconciled. Acquired cash was 184,307 ([10-Q Sep26 p:49]).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Financing, as the notes print it, was 900,000 of 7.125% senior secured notes due February 1, 2033 (issued January 30, 2026), a 1,650,000 senior secured 2026 Term Loan B maturing February 3, 2033, a new revolving credit facility of 500,000 (a 75,000 draw at closing per the December 2025 report), and 800,000 from the sale of 800,000 Series A Cumulative Convertible Participating Preferred Shares at $1,000 per share to the CD&R Investor ([10-Q Sep26 p:10, p:27-28]; [10-Q Dec25 p:10]). Proceeds also refinanced the existing 2024 Term Loan B and paid fees and expenses ([10-Q Dec25 p:10]); fees paid for borrowing on long-term debt were 91,004 in FY2026 ([10-K p:77]). Of the three principal funding pieces (notes, term loan, preferred), debt is 2,550,000 and preferred equity 800,000, so debt is about 76% and the preferred about 24% (derived); the preferred is equity-classified. The 2024 facilities were fully replaced, with no balance on the old revolver at replacement ([10-K p:110]). The new debt issues are the notes and the term loan; the term loan was repriced by 50 basis points on September 21, 2026, and the receivables facility was amended on October 29, 2026 (see CP-1 for terms and amounts). The notes carry a 101% change of control put and optional redemption from February 1, 2029 ([10-K p:110-111]); most covenants are suspended if the notes are rated investment grade by either agency ([10-K p:113]).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The related divestiture is the sale of the U.S. power chain hoist and chain manufacturing operations (Damascus, Virginia and Lexington, Tennessee) to Star Hoist Intermediate, LLC, agreed January 14, 2026 and completed March 4, 2026, which management says the company was required to make to gain regulatory approval; it produced a pre-tax gain of about 103,306 and net cash proceeds of about 183,976, and 193,010 was applied to prepay the term loan ([10-K p:12, p:89]; [10-Q Sep26 p:28]). Transition services of up to six months were provided to the buyer ([10-K p:90]). Use of proceeds therefore combined acquisition funding, refinancing and, after closing, partial deleveraging. Subsequent events inside the cutoff are the term loan repricing, the receivables facility amendment and a planned 150,000 paydown over the next twelve months (see CP-1), the 10,000 working capital payment, and the guidance increase on November 3, 2026. Liquidity effect: total liquidity moved from 561,216 at March 31, 2026 to 531,980 at September 30, 2026 (CP-1). Pro forma information in the annual report states combined net sales of about 2,035,000 for FY2026 and a net loss of about 292,000, as if the acquisition and divestiture had occurred on April 1, 2024, and is unaudited ([10-K p:90]). The commitment papers, purchase agreement, investment agreement, indenture and credit agreement are not supplied, so conditions, termination rights, representations and indemnities cannot be assessed (Insufficient Information).

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: - Revenue durability. Evidence: consumables that "serve safety-critical functions and are characterized by frequent replacement" (Management Language, [10-K p:10]); hardware share of sales 13% versus 8% ([10-K p:11]); legacy growth of 5.3% in Q2 FY2027 ([EX Nov03 p:3]). Mechanic: replacement demand reduces dependence on new capital projects and supports visibility, but hoists and cranes remain tied to industrial capital spending, and the 1.0x book-to-bill shows no order cushion. Credit implication: supportive for debt service stability if the consumables share is as management states; the share is Not disclosed and customer concentration is Not disclosed, so durability is a hypothesis to test, not a finding. Counter: no logged conflict directly counters it; the perimeter change limits comparability. - Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: reported Q2 FY2027 operating margin of about 6.5% (derived from 35,043 over 539,285) against an adjusted EBITDA margin of 20.6% ([EX Nov03 p:13]); H1 FY2027 free cash flow of 4,601 (CP-1). Mechanic: acquisition amortization, step-up costs and integration costs sit between EBITDA and cash earnings, and cash interest is large against operating cash flow. Credit implication: debt service rests on realising synergies and normalising non-cash and one-off costs; if they slip, coverage stays thin. Counter: conflict C5 on deal value does not change this; the Q1 adjusted EBITDA revision of 21 is immaterial. - Investor alignment and control. Evidence: preferred shares rank ahead of common, accrue 7% in cash or in kind, convert to about 43% and give three board seats ([10-K p:49-50, p:130]). Mechanic: the claim accretes ahead of common holders and could become a cash drain if the company elects cash payment or the rate rises to 10%; board seats give influence over strategy and capital allocation. Credit implication: equity cushion beneath the debt is supportive today, but control by an investor whose interests "may be different" requires monitoring of dividends, acquisitions and financing choices; legal capacity is unknown without the documents. Counter: conflict C2 on ownership percentage (42% versus 43%). - Perimeter, integration and concentration risk. Evidence: two perimeter changes within weeks, a business of similar size acquired (the acquired business generated about 1,100,000,000 of revenue in 2024 per [10-Q Dec25 p:9]), preliminary purchase accounting, a 200,000 impairment, and a chief financial officer change ([10-K p:58, p:88]; [10-Q Jun26 p:52]). Mechanic: reporting comparability, control-environment strain and execution load during integration. Credit implication: monitoring posture should stay elevated until two clean quarters of combined reporting and a settled purchase price allocation. Counter: conflicts C1 (revolver maturity) and C5 are open and affect the debt and deal picture. - Key uncertainties. Executed documents, customer concentration, backlog at September 30, 2026, current investor percentage, rating, and the covenant trigger.

rows.label: A US lifting and material-handling manufacturer roughly doubled in size through a debt and preferred-equity funded acquisition. The business is diversified and consumable-linked, but control, governance rights and integration risk now sit with the investor and management.
The acquisition of Kito Crosby on February 3, 2026 was funded by senior secured notes, a term loan and 800,000 of preferred equity.
The preferred investor holds about 43% as-converted, up to three board seats and preemptive rights, and ranks ahead of common shareholders.
Sales are spread across hoists, consumables, conveyors, power controls and actuators, sold mainly through distributors, with about 45% from outside the U.S.
The company has reshaped its portfolio quickly: a regulator-required disposal, a conveyor impairment and a chief financial officer change within the integration period.
Sources disagree on investor percentage, revolver maturity and deal value.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Columbus McKinnon is a leveraged but liquid industrial manufacturer whose credit profile is acceptable only if integration of its February 2026 acquisition delivers the earnings and cash flow management has assumed. Strongest support: a diversified, consumables-linked product base, USD 800.0 million of preferred equity beneath the debt, USD 532.0 million of liquidity and lender-defined net leverage of 4.9x with back-ended term debt maturities. Weakest point: reported earnings and cash flow do not yet carry the capital structure, with first-half cash interest covered only 2.45x and free cash flow of USD 4.6 million. What decides the outcome is synergy delivery, conversion of adjusted EBITDA into cash for the planned USD 150 million paydown, and the conduct of the preferred investor.

What decides the outcome is synergy delivery, conversion of adjusted EBITDA into cash for the planned USD 150 million paydown, and the conduct of the preferred investor.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, the leverage improvement is real in the lender's measure but earned through earnings, not repayment. The company reports a Credit Agreement Net Leverage Ratio of 4.9x at September 30, 2026 against 5.1x at March 31, 2026, while total debt rose from USD 2,393.0 million to USD 2,412.3 million, an increase of USD 19.3 million, and the lender-defined trailing EBITDA rose from USD 441.0 million to USD 467.8 million [Documentary Fact; CP-1 Financials and credit metrics, Calculations]. That trailing figure includes USD 132.4 million (28.3%) of annualised acquisition, divestiture and synergy adjustments, and acquisition-related items together are 66.1% of it; on company-reported adjusted EBITDA without pro forma the same debt is 7.28x gross and 6.95x net [Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the reading; CP-1 Earnings quality and definitions]. For a creditor the mechanism is that leverage tolerance depends on synergies being delivered; a shortfall of 10% in the pro forma figure would add about 0.57x to gross leverage [Analyst Interpretation, derived in CP-1].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Second, cash coverage of the debt service is thin. In the six months to September 30, 2026 adjusted EBITDA was USD 222.6 million against cash interest paid of USD 90.9 million (2.45x), net cash from operations was USD 21.1 million and free cash flow USD 4.6 million, after USD 24.3 million of cash costs related to the acquisition [Documentary Fact; CP-1 Financials and credit metrics, Interpretation]. Management's guidance for fiscal 2027 is adjusted EBITDA of USD 425 million to USD 440 million and interest expense of USD 185 million to USD 190 million, which implies interest cover of about 2.3x at the midpoints, with capital expenditure guided at USD 45 million to USD 55 million [Management Language for guidance; derived in Calculations]. The mechanism is that interest, taxes, integration costs and capital spending absorb most operating cash flow, so the planned USD 150 million paydown within twelve months needs working capital release and synergy savings that are not yet in the cash flow; debt service itself is not at risk on the figures supplied.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Third, liquidity is adequate but concentrated and structurally uncertain. Liquidity was USD 532.0 million at September 30, 2026 (cash USD 110.9 million and USD 421.1 million of revolver availability), down from USD 561.2 million, with no capacity left on the USD 60.0 million receivables facility, which is borrowed by a special-purpose subsidiary, needed a waiver of its delinquency and default ratios at September 30, 2026 and was amended on October 29, 2026 [Documentary Fact; CP-1 Liquidity by facility, Covenants and compliance; CP-1A Corrections to earlier handoffs]. The revolver maturity is stated as 2031 in the latest report and as 2028 in two earlier statements, and the covenant trigger and step-down dates for the first lien leverage test (maximum 7.75x, stepping down to 6.25x) are not supplied, so the liquidity runway and covenant headroom cannot be confirmed [Documentary Fact for the conflict, Insufficient Information for the trigger; CP-0 C1, CP-1 Covenants and compliance]. The mechanism is that one revolver supplies almost all committed undrawn liquidity; a 2028 maturity would put USD 421.1 million of availability about fifteen months out.

facts.text: Fourth, the structure is back-ended but floating-rate heavy. The notes of USD 900.0 million and the term loan of USD 1,449.2 million fall due in February 2033, the receivables facility in August 2028, and the only near-term maturities are planned paydown, small amortisation and a small secured building loan; about USD 586.5 million of floating-rate principal is unhedged against interest rate swaps of USD 965.0 million that begin to mature in March 2027 [Documentary Fact; CP-1 Debt structure, Calculations]. A 100 basis point rise in base rates would cost about USD 5.9 million a year on the unhedged amount (illustrative) [Analyst Interpretation]. Refinancing risk is therefore low before 2028, while interest-rate and hedge-roll risk is a monitoring item.

facts.text: Fifth, business risk is moderate and better diversified than before, but its key supports are partly unproven. The product base spans hoists, lifting and securement consumables, conveyors, power controls and actuators sold through distributors across regions with about 45% of first-half revenue from outside the U.S.; management describes consumables as safety-critical, frequently replaced products, a claim that supports revenue durability if true [Management Language for the consumables claim; CP-1A Company and operating model]. The acquired business is now 55.7% of quarterly net sales, orders and sales grew in the quarter but book-to-bill was 1.0x, and legacy sales growth was 5.3% [Documentary Fact and Management Language; CP-1A]. The mechanism is that cash flow stability depends on replacement demand and industrial activity; customer and distributor concentration and the consumables share are not disclosed, so durability is a hypothesis to monitor, not a finding.

The CD&R Investor holds all 800,000 preferred shares, about 43% as-converted (42% in one earlier report), up to three board seats and preemptive rights; the 7% preferred dividend is accruing in kind, USD 28.6 million through September 30, 2026, and the shares rank senior to common stock [Documentary Fact; CP-1A Ownership and control, CP-1 Claims outside the debt figure]. Debt reduction from divestiture proceeds and equity funding of the deal are supportive actions; the finance chief changed on July 1, 2026 during integration [Documentary Fact; CP-1A Governance and sponsor behaviour]. The mechanism is that the preferred claim accretes ahead of common holders, could turn into a cash drain if the company pays in cash or the rate rises to 10%, and gives the investor influence over capital allocation; creditor consent rights and legal capacity are unknown without the executed documents.

facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: 1. Increase in total debt in the first half of fiscal 2027 = 2,412,308 - 2,393,007 = 19,301 (USD 19.3 million). Increase in lender-defined trailing EBITDA = 467,796 - 441,030 = 26,766. 2. Implied cover at guidance midpoints = adjusted EBITDA midpoint (425 + 440) / 2 = USD 432.5 million divided by interest expense midpoint (185 + 190) / 2 = USD 187.5 million = 2.31x. Interest expense includes non-cash amortisation of financing costs that CP-1 does not quantify, so cash cover would be somewhat higher; guidance is management language and not a forecast made here. 3. Illustrative cash after interest and capital expenditure = 432.5 - 187.5 - capital expenditure midpoint (45 + 55) / 2 = 50.0 gives USD 195.0 million, before cash taxes (USD 25.6 million paid in the first half), working capital, integration cash costs, common dividends and pension contributions. This is arithmetic on guidance, not a free cash flow forecast. 4. 10% shortfall sensitivity (from CP-1): 467,796 x 0.9 = 421,016; 2,412,308 / 421,016 = 5.73x against 5.16x, about 0.57x higher. 5. Unhedged floating principal and rate sensitivity (from CP-1): 1,551,465 - 965,000 = 586,465; 1% of 586,465 = 5,865 (USD 5.9 million a year). 6. Shares of lender-defined EBITDA (from CP-1): 132,389 / 467,796 = 28.3%; (132,389 + 99,441 + 39,889 + 37,563) = 309,282; 309,282 / 467,796 = 66.1%. 7. Kito Crosby share of Q2 FY2027 net sales (from CP-1A) = 300,204 / 539,285 = 55.7%. Debt share of the three main funding pieces = 2,550,000 / 3,350,000 = 76.1%; preferred 23.9% (from CP-1A).

citations.quote: 1. Increase in total debt in the first half of fiscal 2027 = 2,412,308 - 2,393,007 = 19,301 (USD 19.3 million). Increase in lender-defined trailing EBITDA = 467,796 - 441,030 = 26,766.

2. Implied cover at guidance midpoints = adjusted EBITDA midpoint (425 + 440) / 2 = USD 432.5 million divided by interest expense midpoint (185 + 190) / 2 = USD 187.5 million = 2.31x. Interest expense includes non-cash amortisation of financing costs that CP-1 does not quantify, so cash cover would be somewhat higher; guidance is management language and not a forecast made here.

3. Illustrative cash after interest and capital expenditure = 432.5 - 187.5 - capital expenditure midpoint (45 + 55) / 2 = 50.0 gives USD 195.0 million, before cash taxes (USD 25.6 million paid in the first half), working capital, integration cash costs, common dividends and pension contributions. This is arithmetic on guidance, not a free cash flow forecast.
4. 10% shortfall sensitivity (from CP-1): 467,796 x 0.9 = 421,016; 2,412,308 / 421,016 = 5.73x against 5.16x, about 0.57x higher.
5. Unhedged floating principal and rate sensitivity (from CP-1): 1,551,465 - 965,000 = 586,465; 1% of 586,465 = 5,865 (USD 5.9 million a year).
7. Kito Crosby share of Q2 FY2027 net sales (from CP-1A) = 300,204 / 539,285 = 55.7%. Debt share of the three main funding pieces = 2,550,000 / 3,350,000 = 76.1%; preferred 23.9% (from CP-1A).

rows.label: Columbus McKinnon is a heavily indebted but liquid industrial manufacturer early in digesting a transformational acquisition. Credit quality depends on realising synergies and turning earnings into cash to cut debt; investor control adds monitoring risk.
Lender-defined net leverage fell from 5.1x to 4.9x, yet total debt rose by USD 19.3 million in the first half of fiscal 2027.
Cash interest paid in the first half of fiscal 2027 was 2.45x covered by adjusted EBITDA, and free cash flow was USD 4.6 million.
Liquidity of USD 532.0 million is mostly revolver availability, with no capacity left on the receivables facility, which needed a covenant waiver.
The business is diversified by product and region and exposed to consumable replacement demand, but also to industrial cycles and a distributor channel.
The preferred investor holds about 43% as-converted, three board seats and a senior claim to common equity.
Thin cash cover and slow deleveraging
Revolver maturity and covenant mechanics unknown
Cyclical demand, tariffs and raw material cost

spans.text: ## Request

Issuer: COLUMBUS MCKINNON CORP (issuer id cmco; Columbus McKinnon Corporation, New York corporation, Nasdaq: CMCO; the filing registrant and the only reporting entity in the pack). As-of date and cutoff: 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot. Reporting currency named by the run context: USD; the filings state amounts in thousands of US dollars and the earnings releases state amounts in millions or thousands of US dollars. Periods named by the run context: current period q2-2027 (the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2026; the fiscal year ends March 31) and prior period fy-2026 (the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026). Both context periods are confirmed from document content, not file names, in the Sources section below.

Question for this module: can the supplied source set support the requested downstream modules (CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2, CP-5) and what remains blocked? This module gives no credit conclusion, legal interpretation or investment opinion and does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. Source sufficiency is kept separate from completion of downstream analysis.

The run context holds no deal terms, quotes, ratings, peers, precedents, borrower or parent name, guarantors, sponsor, research questions or legal documents (`legal_documents` is "none"). Those blanks are not treated as zero or as evidence.
## Sources

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven supplied filings and releases are enough to run the requested financial, business, synthesis and trace modules with stated limitations. Debt, liquidity, covenant and ownership detail comes only from filing notes and releases. | Medium | No credit agreement, indenture, preferred share terms, purchase agreement, ratings or market data are supplied, so legal terms rest on summaries in filing notes. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| The current-period quarterly report and release are supplied and carry the post-acquisition debt, liquidity and leverage disclosure. | Current capital structure can be sourced from filed statements and notes. | High |

| The annual report contains only about two months of the acquired business, so full-year results are not a like-for-like run rate. | Trend and leverage work must label period and perimeter and use the pro forma and release data with care. | High |

| Several facts conflict or are unresolved: revolver maturity, sponsor ownership percentage, annual report filing date, and the revolver covenant trigger. | Analysts must log each conflict with both locators instead of choosing a value. | Medium |

| Legal documents are absent, and the amended receivables facility terms from late October 2026 are not described. | Covenant headroom, guarantor coverage and receivables-facility triggers cannot be verified against executed terms. | Medium |
### Readiness view

Overall view: READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for the source set as a whole. The pinned filings and releases cover every document family needed for a public-company credit snapshot: an audited annual report for fiscal 2026, three quarterly reports bridging the Kito Crosby close and the current period, and three earnings releases with non-GAAP reconciliations. The current period (quarter ended September 30, 2026) and the prior fiscal year (ended March 31, 2026) named in the context are both directly covered by filed statements. Strongest contrary evidence: legal and financing documents are absent, the acquisition accounting is still preliminary, and the annual report mixes a short post-acquisition stub with full-year legacy results. This view is source sufficiency only (SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY); CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED. It does not assert that quarters are normalized or reconciled, or that any downstream input contract is met.
### Consumer assessments
| Consumer | Readiness | Basis and carried limitations |

| CP-1 (financial data and canonical figures) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Statements, debt, liquidity, cash-flow and cash-paid data are located (see coverage below). Limits: acquisition stub period, preliminary purchase accounting, single reportable segment, discrete fourth quarter only via the June 2026 release, covenant levels for the current facilities only in summary. |

| CP-1A (business and transaction context) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business description, acquisition, financing, preferred equity and divestiture narrative are located in the annual report and quarterly notes. Limits: executed transaction documents absent; sponsor ownership percentage differs between sources; context names no sponsor or parent. |

| CP-2 (fundamental credit synthesis) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Evidence for business and financial risk is located; it draws on the CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs once those exist, and their absence now is not a source condition. Inherits every limitation above; no ratings or market inputs are supplied. |

| CP-5 (evidence trace validator) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Every source is retained and addressable by page, so quotes can be traced. Inherits the conflicts and gaps below; it must treat extraction as text only. |
No consumer is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED. No command in the downstream sheet is DO NOT RUN for source reasons.
### Source coverage by profile
Financial reports (annual and quarterly):

- Statements and period labels. Current-period statements are at [10-Q 2026-09-30 p:5] "Net sales $ 539,285 $ 261,047 $ 1,070,746 $ 496,967" (three and six months, current and prior-year columns). Annual statements and the cash-flow statement are in the annual report ([10-K p:78] "Interest paid $ 45,630 $ 30,054 $ 34,983").

- Debt notes with instrument terms. [10-Q 2026-09-30 p:27-31] cover the Senior Secured Notes, the 2026 Term Loan B, the 2026 Revolving Credit Facility, the AR Securitization Facility, other debt, one finance lease and non-U.S. lines. Annual equivalents are at [10-K p:110-115].
- Liquidity. [10-Q 2026-09-30 p:55] "Our liquidity as of September 30, 2026 was $531,980,000"; the prior year-end figure is stated in the same paragraph.
- Cash paid for interest and taxes. [10-Q 2026-09-30 p:8] "Interest paid $ 90,921 $ 16,114" and the income taxes paid line for the six months.

- Segments. [10-Q 2026-09-30 p:47] "The Company has one operating and reportable segment"; no segment table exists, so segment-level KPIs are not available. Reporting units and goodwill by reporting unit are given at [10-Q 2026-09-30 p:22].

- Acquisition. [10-Q 2026-09-30 p:9] "all-cash transaction valued at $2,821,907,000"; funding by senior secured notes, term loan and preferred shares is at [10-Q 2026-09-30 p:10]. Kito Crosby's contribution to net sales and operating income is stated for the current periods only at the same page. The annual report also carries unaudited pro forma information ([10-K p:90]).

- Financing events after year-end: [10-Q 2026-09-30 p:27] "The AR Securitization Facility was further amended on October 29, 2026" and the First Amendment of September 21, 2026 on the same page; these are subsequent to the quarter for the October event and are inside the cutoff.
- Preferred equity: [10-Q 2026-09-30 p:33] gives the preferred terms in summary and the dividend-in-kind accrual.
- Contingencies: [10-Q 2026-09-30 p:34-43] cover product liability, asbestos and Magnetek matters.
Earnings releases:

- Reported versus adjusted. [EX-99.1 2026-11-03 p:13] "Adjusted EBITDA $ 111,205 $ 40,217 $ 222,648 $ 72,828" with the reconciliation above it; quarter and six-month (year-to-date) columns are labelled separately.

- Credit Agreement leverage. [EX-99.1 2026-11-03 p:14] "Credit Agreement Net Leverage Ratio 4.9x 5.1x" (twelve months ended September 30, 2026 and March 31, 2026) with its Net Debt and trailing adjusted EBITDA build; the definition is at [EX-99.1 2026-11-03 p:15]. This is management's non-GAAP presentation of a defined credit agreement term and does not override filed statements.
- Guidance: [EX-99.1 2026-11-03 p:3] gives updated fiscal 2027 outlook against the prior outlook. It is management forward-looking language, not evidence of results.

- The June 2026 release gives the fourth quarter and fiscal year (three-month and year income statements at [EX-99.1 2026-06-04 p:7-8]; reconciliation at p:14) and is the only source for discrete fourth-quarter figures.

Legal and financing sources: none supplied as documents. The 2026 Credit Agreement, the Senior Secured Notes indenture, the First Amendment, the receivables agreement and amendments, the preferred share terms and the stock purchase agreement appear only as descriptions in filing notes and exhibit lists ([10-K p:113] "The 2026 Credit Agreement and the Senior Secured Notes Indenture (collectively the “Debt Agreements”)"). They remain separate, unsupplied active sources; no later filing collapses them.

Scans, images and decks: none supplied. Presentations are not in the pack; the three earnings releases are text exhibits. The extraction is text only, so charts, images or tables rendered as images, if any, are not inspected (parse gap).
### Entity, perimeter and instrument roles

- Reporting entity: Columbus McKinnon Corporation is the registrant, the Borrower under the 2026 Credit Agreement and the issuer of the Senior Secured Notes ([10-K p:111] "Columbus McKinnon Corporation (the “Borrower”) entered into a new credit agreement"). The statements are consolidated. No separate subsidiary issuer statements are supplied. The 10-Q describes "Columbus McKinnon EMEA GmbH and certain subsidiary guarantors" as parties to the First Amendment ([10-Q 2026-09-30 p:27]); the guarantor list itself is Not supplied, and the context names no guarantors.

- Acquired business: Kito Crosby Limited, acquired from funds associated with KKR ([10-Q 2026-09-30 p:9]); consolidated from February 3, 2026. [10-K p:57] "Please note that the Kito Crosby Acquisition closed on February 3, 2026 so fiscal 2026 includes approximately two months of Kito Crosby financial performance." The U.S. power chain hoist and chain operations were divested on March 4, 2026 (same page), so the annual report perimeter changes twice within the fiscal year.

- Ownership and control: the preferred shares are held by CD&R XII Keystone Holdings, L.P. (the "CD&R Investor", [10-Q 2026-09-30 p:33]). The context leaves sponsor and parent blank; the filings are the only source of this relationship.
- Restricted versus unrestricted entities: not identified in any supplied source (the indenture is absent).
- Currency and units: US dollars; the filings are in thousands and the releases mix millions and thousands, so figure transcription must keep the unit of each source.

- Draft, executed and as-of: all filings are filed statements; the quarterly statements are unaudited; the purchase price allocation is preliminary ([10-Q 2026-09-30 p:11] "The purchase price for the Kito Crosby Acquisition has been preliminarily allocated"). Guidance and "Legacy CMCO" measures are management constructs.
### Version relationships and duplicates

- The pack holds one annual report and three quarterly reports for different periods plus three different releases; none is a duplicate of another. Each quarterly report is a separate active source for its period.

- The December 2025 quarterly report predates the acquisition and describes the pre-acquisition Term Loan B and revolver structure; it does not carry the current capital structure. The annual report describes both the superseded first lien facilities and the 2026 facilities. [10-K p:118] "The key financial covenant is triggered only on any date when any Extension of Credit under the Amended and Restated Revolving Credit Facility is outstanding" describes the superseded revolver, not the 2026 revolver, and must not be read as a current covenant.
- Fiscal year-end quarter: no separate fourth-quarter 10-Q exists, as expected. The fourth quarter appears only in the June 2026 release.
### Conflicts and inconsistencies to carry forward
| ID | Conflict | Locators | Downstream effect |

| C1 | The 2026 Revolving Credit Facility maturity is given as 2028 in one annual report paragraph and in the first-quarter fiscal 2027 quarterly report, and as 2031 in the next annual report paragraph and in the first-quarter and second-quarter fiscal 2027 quarterly reports. | [10-K p:111] "Revolving Credit Facility maturing February 3, 2028"; [10-Q 2026-06-30 p:24] "Revolving Credit Facility maturing February 3, 2028"; [10-K p:112] "maturing February 3, 2031 governed by the 2026 Credit Agreement"; [10-Q 2026-09-30 p:28] "a $500,000,000 2026 Revolving Credit Facility with a group of financial institutions or Revolving Credit Facility maturing February 3, 2031" | Debt maturity profile and liquidity runway need the date logged as conflicting; the latest filing and the second annual paragraph agree on 2031 but the executed agreement is not supplied. |

| C2 | CD&R Investor as-converted ownership is stated as approximately 42% in the December 2025 quarterly report and approximately 43% in the 2026 reports. | [10-Q 2025-12-31 p:10] "approximately 42% of the Company's outstanding equity"; [10-Q 2026-09-30 p:33] "approximately 43% of the Company's outstanding equity following completion of the Kito Crosby Acquisition" | Ownership and control analysis must show both and note the later filing is the more recent statement, without reconciling them. |

| C3 | Annual report filing date: later filings say it was filed on June 2, 2026, but its signature page is dated June 8, 2026 and its cover share count is as of June 4, 2026. | [10-Q 2026-09-30 p:8] "filed with the SEC on June 2, 2026"; [10-K p:164] "Date: June 8, 2026"; [10-K p:2] "outstanding as of June 4, 2026" | Low severity for credit analysis; the as-of timing of annual facts is the March 31, 2026 balance sheet date, but the filing date cannot be fixed from the pack. |

| C4 | The annual report maturity table is introduced as covering three instruments but its total is larger than the three instruments it names. | [10-K p:115] "The principal payments obligated to be made as of March 31, 2026 on the 2026 Term Loan B, the Senior Secured Notes and AR Securitization are as follows:" and "$ 2,440,996" | The maturity wall must be rebuilt from the instrument table, not copied from this total; CP-1 must state what the total includes. Not reconciled here. |
### Strongest contrary evidence and limitations (evidence, risk mechanism, consequence)

- Evidence: the covenant disclosure for the current facilities is a single summary sentence, [10-K p:113] "the key financial covenants prohibit the Consolidated First Lien Leverage Ratio for the reference period ended on such date from exceeding 7.75 to 1.00 as of any date of determination with step-downs for the first three years to 7.25 to 1.00, 6.75 to 1.00 and 6.25 to 1.00." Mechanism: the sources do not state whether the test applies at all times or only when revolver usage passes a threshold (the superseded facility had a usage trigger, [10-Q 2025-12-31 p:25]), nor the step-down dates. Consequence: covenant headroom analysis cannot be completed from the pack; the reported Credit Agreement Net Leverage Ratio is a different, net, all-debt measure from the first lien test and may not be used as covenant headroom.

- Evidence: [10-Q 2026-09-30 p:27] "The Company was in compliance with covenants under the AR Securitization Facility after receiving a waiver of the Delinquency and Default Ratios from the lender effective September 30, 2026." Mechanism: a waiver was needed to avoid breach at the quarter end and the facility was amended again on October 29, 2026, but the new ratio levels and the waived ratio levels are not stated. Consequence: receivables-facility trigger risk is visible but unquantifiable.

- Evidence: the annual report covers only a short post-acquisition stub ([10-K p:57]), and the quarterly reports show a large increase in net sales against prior-year columns. Mechanism: year-over-year and annual comparisons mix perimeters. Consequence: modules must label period and perimeter on every figure and use the pro forma and Legacy CMCO disclosures only as attributed management or unaudited pro forma data.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Leverage is high after the Kito Crosby deal but easing on the lender-defined measure. Reported earnings still carry large deal costs, interest cover is thin, and liquidity is adequate with no large near-term maturities. | Medium | Covenant levels, trigger and the lender-defined earnings build rest on summaries and management adjustments, not executed documents. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Total debt rose in the first half of fiscal 2027 even though the lender-defined net leverage ratio fell from 5.1x to 4.9x. | Deleveraging so far comes from the earnings base and pro forma adjustments, not debt repayment. | High |

| Cash interest paid for the first half of fiscal 2027 was 90,921 against adjusted EBITDA of 222,648. | Cover on a like-for-like six-month basis is thin; floating-rate exposure is partly hedged. | High |

| Liquidity was 531,980 at September 30, 2026, all revolver availability plus cash, with no receivables facility capacity left. | Adequate near-term runway, but the receivables facility needed a waiver and was amended again in late October 2026. | Medium |

| Lender-defined EBITDA of 467,796 includes a large pro forma and synergy add-back, and reported net loss remains large. | Reported leverage is more favourable than a reported-earnings basis, which is far higher. | High |

| Maturities are back-ended: the next 12 months involve about 150,000 of planned paydown, then the term loan and notes fall due in 2033. | No large maturity is scheduled before the receivables facility in 2028, but the revolver date is in conflict and the paydown plan depends on cash generation. | Medium |
### Financial base view

The financial base is usable but must be read in two layers. Reported (GAAP) layer: the business more than doubled in size on the Kito Crosby close (H1 FY2027 net sales 1,070,746 against 496,967 in H1 FY2026), but it is loss-making after amortization, interest and deal costs (H1 FY2027 net loss attributable to the Company 114,262; FY2026 net loss 229,535 including a 200,000 goodwill impairment), operating cash flow is small (H1 FY2027 21,065) and FY2026 operating cash flow was negative (146,211), reflecting acquisition and divestiture related cash payments. Lender-defined layer: the Credit Agreement Trailing Twelve Month Adjusted EBITDA of 467,796 at September 30, 2026 normalises a full year of Kito Crosby, the divestiture and cost synergies, and gives a Credit Agreement Net Leverage Ratio of 4.9x. The first layer is audited or filed; the second is a management reconciliation of a defined credit agreement term and is supporting evidence only. Debt is 2,412,308 (carrying value, including finance lease and the receivables facility) at September 30, 2026, up from 2,393,007 at March 31, 2026. About 1,551,465 of principal is floating rate against 965,000 of interest rate swap notional, so roughly 586,465 is unhedged on the figures supplied. Liquidity is 531,980 with the revolver commitment (500,000) the only meaningful undrawn source. The covenant package (first lien leverage test, maximum 7.75x stepping down) looks roomy against the 4.9x total net measure on an indicative reading, but trigger, step-down dates and exact definition are not supplied, so headroom is not calculable. Confidence in the base is Medium: the filed statements are internally consistent (debt carrying value ties to principal less unamortized costs; the lender-defined EBITDA reconciles line by line), while the credit documents, discrete Q4 FY2026 statements and any ratings are absent.

### Earnings quality and definitions

The Credit Agreement TTM Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation at September 30, 2026 starts from a net loss of (345,759) and adds back, among other items, the annualization of Kito Crosby, the divestiture and synergies of 132,389, goodwill impairment of 200,000, acquisition inventory step-up of 99,441, transaction-related costs of 39,889, acquisition integration costs of 37,563, cost of debt repricing of 25,241, offset by a net gain on sale of business of (102,153) ([EX Nov03 p:14]). The components sum to 467,796 (checked in Calculations). The pro forma and synergy add-back is 28.3% of the lender-defined figure, and the four acquisition-related items together are 66.1% of it (derived). The difference between the lender-defined figure and company-reported LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 331,193 (derived) is 136,603, which management attributes to normalizing for a full year of Kito Crosby, the divestiture and synergies; it is a management estimate, not a reported result. Adjusted EBITDA also adds back stock-based compensation, which is a cost.

Company-reported Adjusted EBITDA for H1 FY2027 is 222,648 in the Q2 release. The Q1 release stated Q1 FY2027 Adjusted EBITDA of 111,464 ([EX Jul30 p:10]) and the Q2 release states Q2 FY2027 of 111,205 ([EX Nov03 p:13]), which sum to 222,669, 21 more than the H1 figure printed; the Q1 figure appears to have been revised by 21 in the later release, without a stated reason (Not supplied).

Reported gross margin (34.8% in Q2 FY2027 per [EX Nov03 p:3], 27.5% in Q1 FY2027 per [EX Jul30 p:2]) is depressed by inventory step-up amortization (acquisition inventory amortization 7,445 in Q2 and 62,643 for the six months, [10-Q Sep26 p:10]); the step-up is a non-cash, non-recurring accounting effect that unwinds as acquired inventory is sold, so gross margin should improve mechanically as it fades.
### Latest quarter and events after quarter end

- Q2 FY2027 (three months to September 30, 2026): net sales 539,285 versus 261,047 (up 106.6%), of which Kito Crosby 300,204 ([10-Q Sep26 p:10]); legacy net sales growth of 5.3% (management Legacy CMCO measure, [EX Nov03 p:13-14]); income from operations 35,043; interest and debt expense 48,050; cost of debt repricing 1,056; pre-tax loss (9,877) with income tax expense of 15,315; net loss attributable to the Company (25,533); acquisition integration and deal expenses 12,465 ([10-Q Sep26 p:5, p:10]). Operating cash flow was negative for the quarter at (4,559), with capital expenditures of 10,796 and free cash flow of (15,355) ([EX Nov03 p:13]).

- Financing events: First Amendment to the 2026 Credit Agreement on September 21, 2026 reduced the term loan and revolver margin by 50 bps; costs of 1,056 and a 279 lender fee ([10-Q Sep26 p:27, p:29]). AR securitization covenant waiver effective September 30, 2026 and amendment on October 29, 2026 (subsequent event, new ratio levels Not supplied).

- Other subsequent events: dividend of $0.07 per common share declared October 26, 2026 (about 2,030, payable November 16, 2026, [10-Q Sep26 p:33]); settlement of a U.S. pension plan after September 30, 2026 ([10-Q Sep26 p:31]); payment of the 10,000 working capital adjustment. Management raised FY2027 guidance on November 3, 2026 to net sales of $2.13 billion to $2.17 billion and Adjusted EBITDA of $425 million to $440 million, with interest expense of $185 million to $190 million and capital expenditures of $45 million to $55 million ([EX Nov03 p:3-4]); this is forward-looking management language.
- Nothing dated after the cutoff 2026-11-05 is used.
### Conflicts, corrections and unresolved differences

- C1 revolver maturity (from CP-0): the latest quarterly report and the second annual paragraph say February 3, 2031 ([10-Q Sep26 p:28]; [10-K p:112]); the first annual paragraph and the June 2026 quarterly report say February 3, 2028 ([10-K p:111]; [10-Q Jun26 p:24]). Both are logged; the 2031 date is used in the tables above because it is the only date in the latest report and appears in the operative revolver paragraph of each report, and the executed agreement is not supplied. The 10-K's own maturity table places no revolver amount in FY2028 (the FY2028 row of 16,500 equals term loan amortization), which fits 2031 (derived). If 2028 were correct the undrawn 421,080 would expire in about 15 months and the 59,644 drawn would fall due then; that would change the maturity wall and the liquidity runway.
- C2 sponsor ownership: approximately 42% in the December 2025 report and 43% in the 2026 reports; not a financial figure and not reconciled here.

- C4 maturity table (from CP-0, extended here): the 10-K table total of 2,440,996 equals the sum of the term loan 1,456,990, notes 900,000, AR facility 53,400, revolver borrowings 25,000 and other debt 5,606 (derived). The sentence introducing the table names three instruments; the arithmetic shows five are included. The finance lease (11,549) is excluded. This is an inference from exact arithmetic, not a source statement.

- Planned paydown versus balance sheet: the notes say about 150,000 of borrowings will be repaid within 12 months and that amount is recorded in current portion, while the balance sheet current portion line is also 150,000 and the same note also states 5,183 of other debt and 851 of finance lease as current. The pack does not show how these reconcile (Not supplied); the 150,000 current portion is used as printed.
- Q1 FY2027 Adjusted EBITDA revised by 21 in the Q2 release (above).
- The 10-K describes the superseded first lien facilities' 3.50x total leverage covenant with a usage trigger ([10-K p:118]); it is not a current covenant and is not used.
### Interpretation: evidence, risk mechanism, credit implication

- Leverage. Evidence: total debt 2,412,308 against Credit Agreement TTM Adjusted EBITDA of 467,796 (5.16x gross; 4.9x on the company's net definition); total debt at March 31, 2026 was 2,393,007. Mechanism: the measured improvement comes from the earnings base growing into the pro forma figure (441,030 to 467,796) and cash rising, not from repayment, and the earnings base includes assumed synergies. Implication: leverage is sensitive to synergy delivery; a shortfall of 10% in pro forma EBITDA would add roughly 0.6x to gross leverage. That sensitivity is derived and illustrative.

- Cover and floating-rate cost. Evidence: H1 FY2027 EBITDA over cash interest of 2.45x; interest and debt expense 95,660 for six months versus FY2027 guidance of 185 to 190 million. Mechanism: floating-rate debt of 1,551,465 with 965,000 hedged leaves about 586,465 exposed to base-rate moves, and the term loan margin was just cut by 50 bps. Implication: a 100 bps rise in base rates would add roughly 5,865 a year on the unhedged amount (derived, illustrative, ignoring the floor and hedge expiries), small against EBITDA but large against free cash flow of 4,601 in H1 FY2027.

- Cash generation. Evidence: H1 FY2027 operating cash flow 21,065 and free cash flow 4,601 after cash deal and integration costs of 24,300 (company-stated for the first half, [EX Nov03 p:3]); cash interest paid 90,921. Mechanism: deal and integration cash costs plus working capital outflows absorb EBITDA. Implication: the planned 150,000 paydown over the next 12 months is not funded by H1 free cash flow; it depends on the second half and on working capital release.

- Liquidity. Evidence: 531,980 at September 30, 2026, down from 561,216; AR facility capacity nil. Mechanism: higher revolver and letters of credit usage. Implication: sufficient on its face for the 12-month needs stated (150,000 paydown, capex guidance of 45 to 55 million), but it is concentrated in one revolver whose covenant trigger is not disclosed.
## Calculations
All inputs are US$ thousands as printed unless stated. Each derived figure shows its inputs; rounding is to the displayed digits.

March 31, 2026: 2,393,007 + 16,067 - 96,562 - 53,127 = 2,259,385; / 441,030 = 5.12 (printed 5.1x). June 30, 2026: 2,376,783 + 18,418 - 98,410 - 51,391 = 2,245,400; / 460,917 = 4.87 (printed 4.9x).

6. LTM company-reported Adjusted EBITDA to September 30, 2026 = FY2026 181,373 - H1 FY2026 72,828 + H1 FY2027 222,648 = 331,193. Total debt / 331,193 = 7.28; net 2,301,408 / 331,193 = 6.95. Difference to the lender-defined figure = 467,796 - 331,193 = 136,603.

7. Interest cover: FY2025 156,751 / 30,054 = 5.22; FY2026 181,373 / 45,630 = 3.97; H1 FY2026 72,828 / 16,114 = 4.52; H1 FY2027 222,648 / 90,921 = 2.45. Q2 FY2027 interest paid = 90,921 - Q1 29,532 [10-Q Jun26 p:7] = 61,389; Q2 EBITDA 111,205 / 61,389 = 1.81 (not charted because Q2 holds the first notes coupon, 900,000 x 7.125% / 2 = 32,063, and Q1 holds none). LTM cash interest to September 30, 2026 = 45,630 - 16,114 + 90,921 = 120,437 (mixed pre- and post-acquisition structure; not used).
13. Change in total debt, H1 FY2027: 2,412,308 - 2,393,007 = 19,301 increase. Change in Credit Agreement TTM Adjusted EBITDA: 467,796 - 441,030 = 26,766 increase.
14. Floating-rate principal = term loan 1,449,233 + revolver 59,644 + AR 42,588 = 1,551,465; less swap notional 965,000 = 586,465; 1% of 586,465 = 5,865.
15. Sensitivity: 10% lower pro forma EBITDA = 467,796 x 0.9 = 421,016; 2,412,308 / 421,016 = 5.73 versus 5.16, an increase of about 0.57.

CP-1A should take the business and transaction context from the same sources and carry forward: the perimeter changes (Kito Crosby from February 3, 2026, divestiture March 4, 2026); the preferred equity (CD&R Investor, conversion price, 7% in kind or cash, ownership percentage conflict C2); and the debt and covenant limits above. ### Reader summary

### Business and transaction view

Columbus McKinnon is a century-and-a-half-old US industrial manufacturer of hoists, lifting and securement hardware, precision conveyors, digital power controls and actuators, sold mainly through distributors and crane builders. On February 3, 2026 it bought Kito Crosby Limited from funds associated with KKR in an all-cash deal, financed by a 900,000 senior secured notes issue, a 1,650,000 term loan, a revolver draw and 800,000 of Series A preferred shares sold to CD&R XII Keystone Holdings, L.P. (the CD&R Investor). To gain regulatory approval it also sold its U.S. power chain hoist and chain operations on March 4, 2026 and used the proceeds to prepay the term loan. The resulting credit profile is a larger, more consumables-weighted business that is loss-making on a reported basis, carries total debt of 2,412,308 at September 30, 2026 and 531,980 of liquidity (the same figures as the CP-1 handoff), and has a large investor with board and preemptive rights whose preferred shares accrue a 7% payment in cash or in kind ahead of common shareholders. Business risk is moderated by breadth of product, brand and geography, and by consumable-type replacement demand that management describes (Management Language); it is raised by cyclical exposure to industrial activity, the distributor channel, the integration of a business of about the same size and a short-tenured finance leadership. Ownership and governance evidence shows supportive documented actions (equity funding, use of divestiture proceeds for debt reduction, in-kind preferred dividends so far) and no documented creditor-adverse or extraction-oriented action, but the legal capacity for such actions depends on credit and indenture documents that are not supplied. Confidence is Medium: the filed business and transaction facts are well sourced, while the executed transaction, investor and financing documents and any customer concentration data are missing.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The transaction is the acquisition of 100% of the equity of Kito Crosby Limited from funds associated with KKR, completed on February 3, 2026 after a definitive agreement announced on February 10, 2025. Status: completed; the purchase price allocation remains preliminary and the working capital adjustment is final. Three figures describe its size and they differ: the December 2025 quarterly report describes an all-cash transaction "valued at $2,700,000,000" subject to customary adjustments and regulatory approval ([10-Q Dec25 p:9]); the annual report's allocation table totals 2,811,907 ([10-K p:88]); and the September 2026 quarterly report states the all-cash transaction value as 2,821,907, which includes a 10,000 increase for the final working capital adjustment, paid after September 30, 2026 ([10-Q Sep26 p:9]). The last two reconcile by the stated adjustment (2,811,907 plus 10,000, derived); the headline-to-consideration difference is not explained in the pack and is logged as a conflict, not reconciled. Acquired cash was 184,307 ([10-Q Sep26 p:49]).

Financing, as the notes print it, was 900,000 of 7.125% senior secured notes due February 1, 2033 (issued January 30, 2026), a 1,650,000 senior secured 2026 Term Loan B maturing February 3, 2033, a new revolving credit facility of 500,000 (a 75,000 draw at closing per the December 2025 report), and 800,000 from the sale of 800,000 Series A Cumulative Convertible Participating Preferred Shares at $1,000 per share to the CD&R Investor ([10-Q Sep26 p:10, p:27-28]; [10-Q Dec25 p:10]). Proceeds also refinanced the existing 2024 Term Loan B and paid fees and expenses ([10-Q Dec25 p:10]); fees paid for borrowing on long-term debt were 91,004 in FY2026 ([10-K p:77]). Of the three principal funding pieces (notes, term loan, preferred), debt is 2,550,000 and preferred equity 800,000, so debt is about 76% and the preferred about 24% (derived); the preferred is equity-classified. The 2024 facilities were fully replaced, with no balance on the old revolver at replacement ([10-K p:110]). The new debt issues are the notes and the term loan; the term loan was repriced by 50 basis points on September 21, 2026, and the receivables facility was amended on October 29, 2026 (see CP-1 for terms and amounts). The notes carry a 101% change of control put and optional redemption from February 1, 2029 ([10-K p:110-111]); most covenants are suspended if the notes are rated investment grade by either agency ([10-K p:113]).

The related divestiture is the sale of the U.S. power chain hoist and chain manufacturing operations (Damascus, Virginia and Lexington, Tennessee) to Star Hoist Intermediate, LLC, agreed January 14, 2026 and completed March 4, 2026, which management says the company was required to make to gain regulatory approval; it produced a pre-tax gain of about 103,306 and net cash proceeds of about 183,976, and 193,010 was applied to prepay the term loan ([10-K p:12, p:89]; [10-Q Sep26 p:28]). Transition services of up to six months were provided to the buyer ([10-K p:90]). Use of proceeds therefore combined acquisition funding, refinancing and, after closing, partial deleveraging. Subsequent events inside the cutoff are the term loan repricing, the receivables facility amendment and a planned 150,000 paydown over the next twelve months (see CP-1), the 10,000 working capital payment, and the guidance increase on November 3, 2026. Liquidity effect: total liquidity moved from 561,216 at March 31, 2026 to 531,980 at September 30, 2026 (CP-1). Pro forma information in the annual report states combined net sales of about 2,035,000 for FY2026 and a net loss of about 292,000, as if the acquisition and divestiture had occurred on April 1, 2024, and is unaudited ([10-K p:90]). The commitment papers, purchase agreement, investment agreement, indenture and credit agreement are not supplied, so conditions, termination rights, representations and indemnities cannot be assessed (Insufficient Information).

### Credit translations

- Revenue durability. Evidence: consumables that "serve safety-critical functions and are characterized by frequent replacement" (Management Language, [10-K p:10]); hardware share of sales 13% versus 8% ([10-K p:11]); legacy growth of 5.3% in Q2 FY2027 ([EX Nov03 p:3]). Mechanic: replacement demand reduces dependence on new capital projects and supports visibility, but hoists and cranes remain tied to industrial capital spending, and the 1.0x book-to-bill shows no order cushion. Credit implication: supportive for debt service stability if the consumables share is as management states; the share is Not disclosed and customer concentration is Not disclosed, so durability is a hypothesis to test, not a finding. Counter: no logged conflict directly counters it; the perimeter change limits comparability.

- Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: reported Q2 FY2027 operating margin of about 6.5% (derived from 35,043 over 539,285) against an adjusted EBITDA margin of 20.6% ([EX Nov03 p:13]); H1 FY2027 free cash flow of 4,601 (CP-1). Mechanic: acquisition amortization, step-up costs and integration costs sit between EBITDA and cash earnings, and cash interest is large against operating cash flow. Credit implication: debt service rests on realising synergies and normalising non-cash and one-off costs; if they slip, coverage stays thin. Counter: conflict C5 on deal value does not change this; the Q1 adjusted EBITDA revision of 21 is immaterial.

- Investor alignment and control. Evidence: preferred shares rank ahead of common, accrue 7% in cash or in kind, convert to about 43% and give three board seats ([10-K p:49-50, p:130]). Mechanic: the claim accretes ahead of common holders and could become a cash drain if the company elects cash payment or the rate rises to 10%; board seats give influence over strategy and capital allocation. Credit implication: equity cushion beneath the debt is supportive today, but control by an investor whose interests "may be different" requires monitoring of dividends, acquisitions and financing choices; legal capacity is unknown without the documents. Counter: conflict C2 on ownership percentage (42% versus 43%).

- Perimeter, integration and concentration risk. Evidence: two perimeter changes within weeks, a business of similar size acquired (the acquired business generated about 1,100,000,000 of revenue in 2024 per [10-Q Dec25 p:9]), preliminary purchase accounting, a 200,000 impairment, and a chief financial officer change ([10-K p:58, p:88]; [10-Q Jun26 p:52]). Mechanic: reporting comparability, control-environment strain and execution load during integration. Credit implication: monitoring posture should stay elevated until two clean quarters of combined reporting and a settled purchase price allocation. Counter: conflicts C1 (revolver maturity) and C5 are open and affect the debt and deal picture.
- Key uncertainties. Executed documents, customer concentration, backlog at September 30, 2026, current investor percentage, rating, and the covenant trigger.

### Corrections to earlier handoffs

- CP-1 stated that all instruments are issued or borrowed by Columbus McKinnon Corporation. The exhibit list of the September 2026 quarterly report names Columbus McKinnon FinCo, LLC as the Borrower under the receivables facility, with the Company as Master Servicer and Performance Guarantor and Wells Fargo Bank, National Association as Lender and Administrative Agent ([10-Q Sep26 p:59]); the amendment to the main credit agreement also names Columbus McKinnon EMEA GmbH and describes agented "Non-EEA" and "EEA" borrowers. The receivables facility is therefore borrowed by a special-purpose subsidiary against U.S. receivables of 93,652 (CP-1), which matters for structural ranking.

- CP-1 listed preferred share ranking and liquidation preference as Not supplied. The annual report states the preferred shares "rank senior to the Company's common shares with respect to dividend rights and with respect to rights on liquidation, winding-up and dissolution" ([10-K p:130]), the rate can rise to 10% if certain events occur ([10-K p:50]) and the investor has board designation and preemptive rights. Still Not supplied: the liquidation preference amount, redemption terms, the rate-increase events and consent rights.
### Consumer readiness

Action: carry each as Insufficient Information; do not treat management consumables language as fact |

| CP-5 (evidence trace validator) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Check figure identity with CP-1 (total debt 2,412,308; liquidity 531,980; preferred carrying 818,403) and the logged conflicts C1, C2, C5, C6 | Cross-module consistency of a multi-perimeter story | Gap: the corrections to CP-1 above. ## Calculations
All inputs are as printed unless stated; US$ thousands.
1. Kito Crosby share of Q2 FY2027 net sales = 300,204 / 539,285 = 55.7% [10-Q Sep26 p:10, p:5].
2. Q2 FY2027 income from operations margin = 35,043 / 539,285 = 6.5% [10-Q Sep26 p:5].

3. Funding mix of the three principal pieces: debt 900,000 + 1,650,000 = 2,550,000; preferred 800,000; total 3,350,000; debt share 2,550,000 / 3,350,000 = 76.1%; preferred share 23.9% [10-Q Sep26 p:10, p:27-28]. The revolver draw of 75,000 is excluded.
5. Backlog attributable to the acquired business = 199,891 / 519,639 = 38.5% [10-K p:15].

7. Conversion shares at issuance: 800,000 / 37.68 = about 21,231 (thousand); the annual report states 21,231,440 [10-K p:49]; in-kind accrual of 28,558 at the same price would add about 758 thousand shares (illustrative, not a disclosed figure, and not used to estimate the percentage).

## Next module

CP-2 should use this handoff for business risk, ownership and governance rows and CP-1 for leverage, liquidity and coverage, and must: name the EBITDA basis for any leverage statement; keep the consumables claim as Management Language; carry the FinCo borrower and the preferred ranking corrections; keep the ownership percentage as 42% versus 43% unresolved; and state the absence of executed documents, customer concentration, backlog at the latest date and ratings as Insufficient Information.
